stories.title: Judge blocks restrictions on foreign student work programs
stories.summary: A federal judge has issued an injunction preventing the administration from enforcing directives that restricted practical training opportunities for international students. The ruling follows a lawsuit from higher education groups, which argued the policies disrupted training programs for students currently attending United States universities on visas.

stories.title: DHS proposes $70,000 fee for student work program
stories.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a $70,000 fee for F-1 visa holders participating in Optional Practical Training. The agency claims the fee will combat fraud and protect American workers. The program was described by a spokesperson as a pipeline for cheap foreign labor.

stories.title: Irish universities report visa-related tuition losses
stories.summary: Four Irish universities expect to lose over €8 million in tuition fees for the 2026/27 academic year following a rise in student visa refusals. Technological University of the Shannon reported that 21 of 24 Indian master's applicants were denied visas, forcing some programs to close.

Federal judge vacates Trump-era student visa limits
stories.summary: A federal judge has struck down a Trump administration rule that would have imposed fixed time limits on international student visas. The court ruled that the Department of Homeland Security failed to adequately justify the changes or consider their consequences. The restrictions will not take effect.

stories.title: Andrew Garson scholarship opens for marketing undergraduates
stories.summary: Marketing executive Andrew Garson has launched a one-time scholarship for undergraduate students pursuing degrees in digital marketing, communications, and business. The award is open to students nationwide, aiming to support emerging talent in modern brand strategy and communications.

stories.title: University of Edinburgh offers full LL.M. tuition scholarship
stories.summary: Edinburgh Law School is offering a full tuition fee waiver for one student pursuing an LL.M. in European and Transnational Law for the 2027 to 2028 academic year. The scholarship is open to both UK and international applicants, including Indian law graduates and lawyers.

stories.title: Erasmus Mundus scholarship offers monthly support for law students
stories.summary: The European Master in Law and Economics has opened applications for its 2027 to 2028 programme. Selected students may receive Erasmus Mundus scholarships providing up to €1,400 per month. The one-year postgraduate course is open to law and economics graduates from various countries, including India.

stories.title: Indiana scholarship provides up to $40,000 for future teachers
stories.summary: Governor Mike Braun is promoting the Next Generation Hoosier Educators Scholarship, which offers up to $10,000 annually for four years of college. Recipients must commit to teaching in Indiana for at least five years. Nearly 90 percent of the program's first cohort remain in the classroom.

stories.title: HEC announces Chinese government scholarship programme for Pakistani students
stories.summary: The Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan has announced the Chinese Government Scholarship Programme (Type-A) for the academic year 2027-28, inviting applications from talented Pakistani students to pursue higher education in leading Chinese universities. The scholarship programme, offered by the China Scholarship Council (CSC), Government of China, aims to promote

stories.title: Global Schools Group opens applications for 2027 scholarship
stories.summary: The Global Schools Group has announced its 2027 Global Citizen Scholarship, offering fully funded places for students to complete their final two years of secondary school at its Singapore campus. The program targets academically talented students from across India.

stories.title: Pakistan HEC opens applications for 61 Chinese government scholarships
stories.summary: The Higher Education Commission of Pakistan is accepting applications for 61 Chinese Government Scholarships for the 2027 to 2028 academic year. The awards cover undergraduate, master’s, and PhD studies at Chinese universities. The commission will act as the nominating agency for all candidates.

stories.title: HEC Pakistan opens GRE training for PhD scholarship applicants
stories.summary: The Higher Education Commission of Pakistan has opened registration for in-person GRE training sessions in five cities. The training is part of the US-Pakistan Knowledge Corridor PhD Scholarship Programme. Eligible nationals must submit their applications through the official portal by December 13.

stories.title: Airtel Foundation opens applications for tech scholarship
stories.summary: The Airtel Foundation is accepting applications for its N100 million Tech Scholarship until December 3, 2026. The program plans to award N500,000 each to 100 undergraduate students studying ICT-related disciplines. The initiative supports high-performing students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.

stories.title: Nebraska ranks No. 37 in undergraduate entrepreneurship
stories.summary: The University of Nebraska to Lincoln earned the 37th spot in global undergraduate entrepreneurship rankings from The Princeton Review and Entrepreneur magazine. The university remains the top-ranked institution in the state and 24th among public universities. The school says it prepares students to become entrepreneurs and innovators.

stories.title: Stockholm University rises in sustainability rankings
stories.summary: Stockholm University reached 70th place in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings, scoring 93.5 out of 100 points. The university ranked 3rd globally for research and 11th for education related to sustainable development. It is currently the 6th highest-ranked university in Sweden.

stories.title: University of the Philippines leads local institutions in sustainability
stories.summary: The University of the Philippines ranked 443rd in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings, placing it first among 11 Philippine institutions. The country's representation in the list increased from eight universities last year to 11 this year. Ateneo de Manila University followed at 477th place.

stories.title: Two Canadian universities reach global top 10 for sustainability
stories.summary: The University of Toronto and the University of British Columbia placed in the top 10 of the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings. The list evaluated over 2,000 universities across 107 locations. The University of British Columbia climbed to fourth place globally, up from fifth last year.

stories.title: IIT-Kanpur ranks 315th in sustainability
stories.summary: IIT-Kanpur achieved 315th place in the 2027 QS World University Ranking for Sustainability. The institute scored 79.6 points, with 91.4 in employability and 89.1 in knowledge exchange. IIT-Delhi remains the highest-ranked Indian institution on the list, holding the 194th global position.

stories.title: IIT Delhi enters global top 200 for sustainability
stories.summary: IIT Delhi reached 194th place in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings, becoming the top-ranked Indian institution. The university increased its overall score to 86.5 and established a task force to monitor campus operations. It previously held the 205th position in the global rankings.

stories.title: UST improves global standing in sustainability rankings
stories.summary: The University of Santo Tomas climbed 24 spots to 810th in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings. It was the only Philippine institution to improve its global standing this year. The university also reached 423rd globally in governance, the highest rank for any local institution in that category.

stories.title: VIT University reaches 293rd in global sustainability rankings
stories.summary: Vellore Institute of Technology secured 293rd place globally and 5th in India in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings. The university scored 81.2 overall, an improvement of 59 places from its previous rank of 352nd. The rankings assess environmental impact, social impact and governance.

stories.title: IIT Delhi improves sustainability ranking
stories.summary: IIT Delhi climbed 11 places to 194th in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings. The institute's overall score rose to 86.5, and it advanced to 19th place within Asia. Officials stated that a sustainability task force now coordinates campus operations and monitors progress toward measurable outcomes.

stories.title: McGill ranks 12th globally in sustainability
stories.summary: McGill University tied for 12th place worldwide in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings. The school ranked 5th in North America and first in the region for the impact of education. The university says it is grateful to colleagues for integrating sustainability into the curriculum.

stories.title: U of G Recognized Among North America’s Leading Universities for Sustainability - U of G News
UBC reaches fourth place in sustainability rankings
stories.summary: The University of British Columbia ranked fourth globally in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings. The university received near-perfect scores in environmental education and research. It placed second among 399 institutions in the Americas and second among 39 Canadian universities included in the report.

stories.title: Johns Hopkins forms committee to expand enrollment
stories.summary: Johns Hopkins University has formed an advisory committee to increase undergraduate enrollment. The university currently reports one of the smallest undergraduate class sizes among its peers, with 6,354 students enrolled in fall 2025. The move aligns with the university's 2023 Ten for One framework.

stories.title: Birmingham pauses Shakespeare Institute relocation
stories.summary: The University of Birmingham has paused plans to move the Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-upon-Avon. Vice-chancellor Adam Tickell granted a six-month reprieve following a petition that gained 10,000 signatures. The university has not ruled out the relocation, stating it will reassess options during the delay.

stories.title: Panjab University hosts lecture on UGC NET
stories.summary: The Department of Political Science at Panjab University held a lecture on strategies for the UGC NET examination. The event featured alumni speakers and focused on guidance for students pursuing careers in teaching and research. The university described the exam as a key national-level opportunity.

stories.title: Sunderland expands two-year degree offerings
stories.summary: The University of Sunderland is adding business, law and criminology to its two-year accelerated degree programs. The university claims these courses provide the same quality of teaching as traditional three-year routes. The University of Buckingham has offered similar accelerated degrees since the 1970s.

stories.title: NUS president criticizes changes to international student rules
stories.summary: NUS president Amira Samuel warned that frequent changes to rules for international students are damaging the reputation of UK higher education. Speaking at an event, she argued that institutions should not alter terms after payments have been made. She described the current approach as a broken promise.

stories.title: Richmond provost opposes return to in-person exams
stories.summary: Kelly Coate, provost of Richmond American University London, stated that mandating in-person exams to counter AI use would be the worst response for the sector. The comments follow guidance from the Office for Students, which encouraged in-person testing after finding widespread AI use among students.

stories.title: States urge Nilekani panel to ease NEET-UG pressure with Class 12 marks, multiple attempts - Telegraph India
Universities urged to find sweet spot in industry partnerships
stories.summary: W. John Kao, president of National Tsing Hua University, told a Seoul summit that aligning special interests between universities, industry, and government creates a win, win, win situation. He advised leaders to drill down into key performance indicators to find a sweet spot where everyone walks away happy.

stories.title: States propose NEET UG exam reforms
stories.summary: Several states have suggested incorporating Class 12 board marks into NEET UG scores and moving to a computer-based testing format. These proposals were presented to the Nandan Nilekani-led task force on exam reforms, which has had its tenure extended until January 2027 while deliberations continue.

stories.title: Australian universities face new racism regulations
stories.summary: A new regulatory standard requires Australian universities to guarantee a safe environment that prevents and responds to racism. The sector has expressed concern over being singled out for these responsibilities by a government whose own international education policies may be contributing to the polarization of minority groups.

stories.title: States push for NEET UG changes
stories.summary: State governments have asked the Nandan Nilekani-led task force to consider multiple annual attempts for the NEET UG exam and the inclusion of Class 12 marks in final results. The proposals aim to reduce reliance on a single high-stakes entrance test. The task force is currently reviewing options.

stories.title: Oxford protest planned against visiting academic
stories.summary: Thousands have signed a petition against an Oxford University event featuring Nathan Cofnas, an academic previously suspended by the University of Ghent. Cofnas has drawn criticism for his views on race and intelligence. The university has not commented on the planned protests.

research.title: Synthetic Doubt and the Integrity of Digital Proof before the International Criminal Court
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence complicates evidentiary assessment at the International Criminal Court by enabling fabricated audiovisual material and making authentic digital evidence easier to dismiss as fake. This article calls the latter problem synthetic doubt: an objection. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Who Bears the Excess? Imputing the Acts of AI Agents to Those Who Delegate
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: When an AI agent acts outside the authority conferred on it, the actor is not a legal subject and the legal subjects did not act. The literature of 2026 agrees that the agent cannot bear responsibility. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
